stories.title: Deepfake victim urges better regulation of 'dangerous' AI
stories.simple_summary: Someone who had a fake video made of them using AI is asking for stronger rules to stop this from happening to others. Deepfakes are fake videos created by AI that look real but aren't.
stories.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know could become a victim of a fake video used to trick or embarrass them, better rules might help protect you — but this is still an area where laws are catching up to technology.

stories.title: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI paused work on a new AI model called Astra because it got too powerful — the AI could figure out how to break into computer systems on its own, which is dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to technology experts and investors — it shows AI companies are trying to be careful, but it doesn't affect you directly right now.

stories.title: After Rippling blew millions on AI in months, it built an employee ROI tool
stories.simple_summary: A company called Rippling spent a lot of money on AI tools without tracking whether they were actually helping, so they built a tool to track which employees are using AI and how much it costs.
stories.why_it_matters: If your business uses AI tools, this is a reminder to check whether you're actually getting your money's worth from them instead of just using them because they're trendy.

stories.title: ‘SaaSpocalypse’ debate intensifies as software stocks swing wildly
stories.simple_summary: Software company stocks (the pieces of ownership you can buy) are going up and down wildly, and people are debating whether this is a bubble about to pop.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — if you don't own software stocks, nothing changes for your business or life.

stories.title: Fenix Flexin isn’t even denying using AI to make ‘Rubberz’ anymore
stories.simple_summary: A rapper admitted he used an AI tool to help create his song instead of making it himself. The AI company even released a tool that can tell when AI made a song.
stories.why_it_matters: If you care about music, entertainment, or art being made by actual humans, this is a sign that AI is being used to create things we used to think required human talent.

stories.title: Watching Roku’s AI channel is like eating from a trough
stories.simple_summary: Roku (a TV streaming service) created a channel that just plays AI-generated videos instead of real movies and shows — like getting food from a trough instead of a real meal.
stories.why_it_matters: If you watch streaming TV, this is just one experimental service — you probably still have plenty of real entertainment choices, but it shows AI is creeping into places you might not expect.

stories.title: OpenAI puts the brakes on a new model because it’s supposedly too powerful
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI is slowing down work on a new AI model called Astra because it's too powerful and might be dangerous until they can make it safer. Other AI companies have also had similar problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech professionals and investors — it shows AI safety is becoming a real concern, but it doesn't affect your daily life right now.

stories.title: What’s behind the Google AI shake-up
stories.simple_summary: Some important people who worked on AI at Google either left Google or moved to different jobs, which might mean Google is falling behind companies like OpenAI in the AI race.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people in tech — if you use Google products, you probably won't notice a change, but it suggests Google might be struggling in AI development.

stories.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
stories.simple_summary: A company called Cloudflare built a new browser (the program you use to look at websites) designed to work with AI robots instead of people. It uses less computer power than regular browsers.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to programmers and tech companies building AI tools — nothing you need to worry about as an ordinary business owner right now.

stories.title: Opinion | Don't Anthropomorphize Artificial Intelligence
stories.simple_summary: An opinion article warns people not to talk about AI as if it thinks or feels like a human, because it doesn't.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a reminder to be realistic about what AI can and can't do — don't assume it's smarter or more conscious than it actually is.

stories.title: Airbnb says AI is helping it ship features faster as it tests a new search function
stories.simple_summary: Airbnb is using AI to help its engineers build new features faster, and they're testing a new way for people to search for rentals using AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Airbnb, you might see a slightly better search experience soon, but this is mostly a behind-the-scenes change.

stories.title: Jill Lepore on the ‘Artificial State’ and why Silicon Valley’s leaders are bad sci-fi readers
stories.simple_summary: A historian named Jill Lepore wrote a book about how tech company leaders use grand, government-like language when describing their products, often in ways that sound better than they should.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly cultural commentary — a reminder to be skeptical when tech companies use big dramatic language about their products rather than just explaining what they actually do.
